clue.text: Livelihood of a cleaner, supported by money

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: a daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's income comes from what she is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British domestic cleaner; the phrase comes from the Lord's Prayer's 'give us this day our daily bread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily bread is an idiom for the basic earnings a person lives on.

explanation.surface: A master of language finds himself speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome is to master; overcome also means so moved one cannot speak.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: taken as written
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone is surely party to the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic adverb of agreement, a synonym for certainly.

explanation.surface: A levy charged on products and on the service given.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a tax on imports, and also a service one is obliged to perform.

parts.note: a dressing spread on a field matters because it helps crops grow, not a military bandage

explanation.surface: A battlefield bandage that is becoming ever more vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field dressing' is a soldier's emergency bandage, but here it is something dressed on farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure or chemical feed spread on fields to make plants grow is exactly this substance.

clue.text: Imply port swallowed is of a lower standard

indicators.note: the port is taken inside the verb, as food is swallowed

parts.note: infer is loosely used to mean imply or suggest
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is often just Rio

explanation.surface: Suggesting that the port wine drunk was not up to scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means worse or lower in quality, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Parents separated by an ascending waterway

indicators.note: the two parents are pushed apart with a piece placed between them

parts.note: pa and ma are both parents

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the short word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Mother and father parted by a waterway climbing uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascending' works only because this is a down entry, so the short word reads upwards; the definition leans on the Panama Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal is the famous waterway, named after the country it crosses.

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel or barge

explanation.surface: A call shouted to a passing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the sailor's shout used to greet or call to another vessel.

indicators.note: one piece set beside the other in sequence

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Taking a chance by travelling along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a North Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is a hazardous undertaking, a venture that involves risk.

explanation.surface: A Welsh town described in verse as second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neath is a poetic shortening of beneath, meaning below; Neath is also a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic contraction means below or lower; Neath is a town near Swansea in south Wales.

parts.note: read not as feeling insulted but as the crime of taking property

explanation.surface: Being upset at a slight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking offence' means being hurt, but read it as an offence that consists of taking.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, the offence of taking another's goods.

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: they refers to those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: Treating those patients for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' reads as free of cost, but 'without' here has its old meaning of outside, so the people wrap round the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal, a near synonym for cure.

clue.text: It may be in the bank or in circulation

definitions.text: It may be in the bank or in circulation

parts.words: It may be in the bank or in circulation
parts.note: sounds like money, but means a fluid stored in a donor bank or pumped round the body

explanation.surface: Something that might be deposited or else in general use, like cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks and circulation suggest money; a blood bank stores donations and blood circulates round the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fluid is kept in blood banks and moves through the circulatory system.

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a hollow in the ground
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: Thrashing a mate till he is empty, then eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is for the heart to beat rapidly or flutter.

clue.text: Men on phone exchange will be a rarity

indicators.note: a telephone exchange in the surface, but as a verb it tells us to swap the letters around

explanation.surface: Men answering the phone at the exchange would be an unusual sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be a remarkable or exceptional thing, something rare.

parts.note: the Baker Street detective calls a simple case by this word, telling Watson it was easy

explanation.surface: Nothing is too hard for the detective at his London address.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes lived at 221B Baker Street, London, and is popularly quoted as saying 'my dear Watson' after this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and simple, so no problem at all, as Holmes famously says.

clue.text: His Christmas present was one of three

definitions.text: His Christmas present was one of three

parts.words: His Christmas present was one of three
parts.note: not a gift but the Ghost of Christmas Present, one of three spirits visiting a miser in Dickens

explanation.surface: Someone who received one of three gifts at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol the miser is visited by the ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is haunted by three spirits, one being Christmas Present.

clue.text: I came up to brew tea and dry up

indicators.note: in a down clue the words are read upwards, so backwards
brewing tea stirs it into a new mix, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arriving to make a cuppa and do the drying-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses I CAME to EMACI, and 'brew' turns TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to waste away or make abnormally thin, shrivelling as if dried.

indicators.note: used as a verb, to work something is to knead or shape it into a new form

explanation.surface: A factory hand whose productivity is low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work rate' reads as one phrase, but 'work' is the anagram signal for RATE POOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is a person who runs a machine, as a machinist does.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone strangely in love with how they look.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is a person's outward manner or bearing, how they appear.

clue.text: Clean up on the favourite, darling!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: to mop up is to clean up spills
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A bettor cleans up on the favourite and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a punter's winnings; MOP is 'Clean up' and the pet sits under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moppet is an affectionate word for a small child, a little darling.

clue.text: Its happy ending comes as a relief

definitions.text: Its happy ending comes as a relief

parts.words: Its happy ending comes as a relief
parts.note: relief here is the military lifting of a blockade on a town, which ends it happily

explanation.surface: A story whose happy ending is a great relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief is the arrival of forces that break a blockade of a town, as in the Relief of Mafeking.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege of a town ends happily for the defenders when it is relieved.

clue.text: A sleeping partner who was robbed of his capital assets

definitions.text: A sleeping partner who was robbed of his capital assets

parts.words: A sleeping partner who was robbed of his capital assets
parts.note: not a business investor, but a biblical strongman whose hair was cut while he slept beside Delilah

explanation.surface: A silent investor in a firm who was swindled out of his money.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is a silent investor; capital is the head, its assets the hair Delilah had cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: In Judges, the strongman lost his power when Delilah had his hair shorn as he slept.

clue.text: Upset glue, lid needs to be put on first

indicators.text: needs to be put on first
indicators.note: the lid comes before the glue in the answer, placed at the front

parts.note: a cap is a lid
size is a gluey sealant used on paper or plaster

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pot of adhesive: replace the top before it spills.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to overturn a boat, to upset it.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
W and S stand for west and south, compass directions

explanation.surface: Livestock under strict instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows are female cattle, the commonest kind seen on farms.

clue.text: He is trained in horse jumping

definitions.text: He is trained in horse jumping

parts.words: He is trained in horse jumping
parts.note: not a show-jumper on a mount but an athlete leaping the vaulting horse

explanation.surface: A rider who has learned show-jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse is the vaulting horse in a gymnasium, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts train on apparatus including the vaulting horse and pommel horse.

explanation.surface: A gift of talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a present, and also a natural talent or ability.

indicators.note: the word for peace is spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: rest is peace and quiet

explanation.surface: Resorting to violence in the cause of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull or seize something by force.

clue.text: Seen by footballer shown the red card? Well, no!

definitions.text: Seen by footballer shown the red card?

explanation.surface: A footballer sent off sees red and feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: A red card sends a player off, so that is the colour he sees as he goes; 'Well, no' means not well.
explanation.definitionFit: Off colour is an idiom for feeling slightly ill; red is the sending-off colour.
